item.title: World Literacy Day
item.description: Children in Tonga came together this week, 8 September, to celebrate International Literacy Day through a special reading event highlighting the importance of literacy, language and inclusive learning. The event was hosted by Save the Children Australia and the Ministry of Education and Training ( MET ), in partnership with the Global Partnership for Education ( GPE ).
item.content:encoded:
Children in Tonga came together this week, 8 September, to celebrate International Literacy Day through a special reading event highlighting the importance of literacy, language and inclusive learning.

The event was hosted by Save the Children Australia and the Ministry of Education and Training ( MET ), in partnership with the Global Partnership for Education ( GPE ).

The programme included English poems presented by Meleane, a Year 4 student from GPS Mu’a; and Simione, a Year 6 student from GPS Fasi; on the themes of healthy living, wellbeing and drug awareness, alongside a Tongan language reading focused on literacy. The readings were accompanied by sign language interpretation, reinforcing the importance of ensuring learning opportunities are accessible to all children.

A Tongan reading was also presented through a speech on Literacy, by Year 6 student from Hilliard Memorial School, Fiapa’i.

During a discussion of recent Pacific Islands Literacy and Numeracy Assessment ( PILNA ) results, education stakeholders reflected on literacy outcomes in Tonga and the importance of continued action to strengthen foundational learning. The results highlighted both progress and ongoing challenges, reinforcing the need for sustained investment in literacy, quality learning materials and effective teaching practices to ensure all children can reach their full potential.

Director for Primary School Division, Mr Herbert Takeifanga, emphasised the importance of literacy in supporting children's learning and future success.

" Reading is the foundation of learning. When children develop strong literacy skills in their early years, they are better equipped to succeed throughout their education and beyond. Every child in Tonga deserves access to quality books and learning opportunities that inspire a lifelong love of reading. International Literacy Day reminds us that investing in literacy is an investment in our children's future and the future of our nation."

In Tonga, only 30% of Year 6 students reach the minimum reading standard, demonstrating the need for continued investment in literacy and foundational learning.

Through a partnership between the Education ( MET ), GPE , Save the Children and Library For All, Tonga is expanding access to reading materials that reflect local culture and experiences. The initiative is expected to deliver more than 300 book titles for Years 1-6, with approximately 40,000 books planned for distribution throughout Tonga.

Save the Children Tonga Country Lead, Lilieta Takau, said literacy remains fundamental to every child's education journey.

" The progress we are seeing in literacy has been made possible through strong partnerships and investment in education. However, there is still much work to do. As governments and development partners consider future education investments, it is critical that foundational literacy remains a priority. Every investment in reading is an investment in a child's future."

International Literacy Day is celebrated globally on 8 September each year. This year's theme, 'Literacy for People, the Planet and Prosperity', recognises the critical role literacy plays in creating opportunities for individuals, communities and nations.
